muffin.prep: Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners (or grease it lightly).
muffin.cook: Divide the batter evenly between the muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full. Bake at {temp} for {time}, until the tops are golden.
muffin.check: A toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin should come out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
notes: Ovens differ - start checking at the early end of the range.
Rest the muffins in the tin for 5 minutes before moving them to a wire rack.

muffin.prep: Set heat-safe paper or silicone muffin cups in the air fryer basket, a few at a time, leaving space between them.
muffin.cook: Spoon the batter into the cups, filling each about 2/3 full. Air fry at {temp} for {time}, until risen and golden.
muffin.check: A toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin should come out clean or with a few moist crumbs. If the tops brown too fast, cover loosely with foil.
notes: Air fryers run hot and vary a lot - check around the 12-minute mark.
Use cups that fit your basket, and weigh down loose paper liners so they cannot lift toward the heating element.

muffin.prep: Set heat-safe silicone or foil cups in a steamer basket or on a rack, leaving space between them. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel so water does not drip onto the muffins.
muffin.cook: Fill each cup about 2/3 full. Cover and steam at a steady medium steam for {time}. Do not lift the lid during the first 10 minutes.
muffin.check: A toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin should come out clean. Steamed muffins stay pale and very soft.
notes: Steamed muffins do not brown - that is normal.
Keep the water at a steady simmer and top it up with hot water if it runs low.

recipes.name: Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: Soft, golden muffins bursting with juicy blueberries.

yield.note: Based on a standard 12-cup muffin tin.

less.note: Blueberry muffins stay soft and tender with about 25% less sugar, and the berries add their own natural sweetness.
expectedChanges: May brown slightly less on top
Crumb may be a touch less moist and tender

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine - overmixing makes tough muffins.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the muffins cool for a few minutes before serving. They are best the day they are made.

tips: Use frozen blueberries straight from the freezer - do not thaw them, or the batter turns purple.
Stir only until the flour disappears. A few lumps are fine and keep muffins tender.
Room-temperature eggs and milk blend more evenly into the batter.

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Muffins
recipes.description: Bakery-style muffins studded with melty chocolate chips.

yield.note: Based on a standard 12-cup muffin tin.

less.note: The chocolate chips bring plenty of sweetness, so about 25% less sugar in the batter is rarely noticed.
expectedChanges: May brown slightly less on top
Crumb may be a touch less tender

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine - overmixing makes tough muffins.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the muffins cool for a few minutes before serving. They are best the day they are made.

tips: Toss the chips in a spoonful of the measured flour so they do not all sink to the bottom.
Save a few chips to sprinkle on top for a bakery look.
Do not overmix - stir just until no dry flour remains.

recipes.name: Banana Muffins
recipes.description: Moist, naturally sweet muffins made with ripe bananas.

yield.note: Based on a standard 12-cup muffin tin.

less.note: Ripe bananas supply lots of natural sweetness, so this recipe tolerates about 30% less sugar very well.
expectedChanges: May brown slightly less on top
Muffins stay moist thanks to the banana

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, mash the ripe bananas well, then whisk in the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the muffins cool for a few minutes before serving.

tips: The riper the bananas (lots of brown spots), the sweeter and moister the muffins.
Freeze overripe bananas whole and thaw them before mashing.
Do not overmix - stir just until combined.

recipes.name: Apple Cinnamon Muffins
recipes.description: Warmly spiced muffins with tender pieces of apple.

yield.note: Based on a standard 12-cup muffin tin.

less.note: The apples and cinnamon carry a lot of flavor, so about 25% less sugar still tastes good.
expectedChanges: May brown slightly less on top
Crumb may be a touch less moist

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Fold in the diced apple.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the muffins cool for a few minutes before serving.

tips: Dice the apple small (about 1 cm / 1/2 in) so it cooks through in the muffin.
Firm, slightly tart apples such as Granny Smith keep their shape best.
Toss the diced apple with a pinch of cinnamon before folding it in.

recipes.name: Vanilla Muffins
recipes.description: A simple, tender base muffin that welcomes any add-in.

yield.note: Based on a standard 12-cup muffin tin.

less.note: Plain muffins rely on their sugar for flavor, so this recipe is reduced by a moderate 25%.
expectedChanges: May brown slightly less on top
Crumb may be a touch less tender

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine - overmixing makes tough muffins.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the muffins cool for a few minutes before serving. They are best the day they are made.

tips: This is a great base for add-ins: try blueberries, chocolate chips or cinnamon.

A spoonful of yogurt or sour cream in place of some milk makes them extra soft.
